doc.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023

title: Young players and the internet
summary: Students today learn solos by slowing down records and are far more advanced than Marini was.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: If you were in front of — you’ve probably done this — being in front of like career day at a college level, do students, do you run into jazz snobs and do they even know what questions to ask about a potential career in this business?

Well yeah you do, but kids today seem very savvy because the internet allows them to not only listen to — you know in my day, Randy Brecker and I have talked about this, we were taking solos off records by playing them over and over again and learning the solo in real time. Now kids can do the slow-down, they can take a Cannonball Adderley solo and they have a choice of dozens, and then slow it down, learn the solo, learn what Cannonball does and then speed it up. I hear kids today that are so much more advanced than I was when I was their age. Kids 18, 17, who are already players. You know they can play.
The same thing happened to me, and they come in as freshmen and I go hmmm, I’m going to have to up my game here.
